title: Courtyard shade exhibit
brief:
Complete the following real project in the current, initially empty directory. Choose the deliverables, media, tools, structure and implementation that serve the intended user. Build usable artifacts and check your work. Deliver the project itself. Omit personally identifying credits, author signatures and model or toolchain identity labels. No network access or credentials are provided.

Produce a small exhibit for apartment residents comparing how shade moves across their shared courtyard. The display will hang by the mailboxes during a two-week vote on where to put a movable reading bench. Fictional observations from a single clear June day record shaded area at 9 a.m., noon, and 4 p.m. as follows: gate alcove 80%, 25%, 10%; fig tree 35%, 70%, 85%; west wall 15%, 20%, 75%. Residents usually pause for under a minute. Choose visual and participation materials that fit a board 90 cm wide and allow residents to mark a preferred location.

files.body:
# Mounting the courtyard bench vote

Print both pages of **Courtyard bench exhibit.pdf** single-sided on A3 paper, portrait, at actual size. Use uncoated paper so pencil marks show clearly. Print a spare copy of page 2.

Write the closing date and time on the voting sheet, two weeks after opening. Mount the shade survey on the left and the voting sheet on the right, with a 2 cm gap. The pair measures **61.4 cm wide × 42 cm high**, leaving about 14 cm on each side when centered on the 90 cm board. Place the voting circles within reach of seated residents. Attach a sharpened pencil on a cord long enough to reach every row.

Each location has 38 circles. If any row fills, save the marked sheet and put up the spare with the same closing date. At closing, count marked circles for each location across all sheets and post the three totals by the mailboxes.

files.body:
# Courtyard reading bench exhibit

## Print and mount

1. Print both pages of `Courtyard-exhibit.pdf` in color on separate A3 landscape sheets. Select **Actual size** or **100%**.
2. Hang the shade comparison on the left and the voting sheet on the right. With a 1 cm gap, the two sheets use **85 cm of width × 29.7 cm of height**, leaving 2.5 cm on each side of a 90 cm board when centered.
3. Fill in the opening and closing dates for the two-week vote. Attach a dark pen beside or below the voting sheet and mount it where residents can comfortably reach the circles.

## Run the vote

Each resident marks one empty circle beside their preferred location. The voting sheet holds 54 marks per location. If a row fills, write the same dates on a fresh copy of page 2, swap it in, and keep the original for counting.

At closing, take down the voting sheet and count one vote per marked circle. Add the counts for each location across all sheets used.
